title: Energy Supplier Switch — Shared Rental Property
goal: Consumer successfully switches energy provider for a shared rental property, from initial research through first bill confirmation, with no gap in supply and fair bill-splitting established
summary: A universal service mission capturing the end-to-end experience of switching energy provider for a shared rental property. The graph covers discovering the need to switch, researching and comparing tariffs, coordinating housemate agreement, completing registration, passing verification, and establishing ongoing account management. Multiple personas can flow through this mission, each generating their own Experience artifact.

scope.trigger: Rate increase notification or discovery that current tariff is uncompetitive
scope.completion: First bill received and ongoing payment routine established
scope.timeframe: 2-4 weeks from initial research to first bill

successCriteria.target: Account active with no supply gap

laneContent.description: Consumer begins the energy switching journey
Consumer receives notification from current provider about rate increase, prompting investigation into switching options

channels.name: Email notification
channels.usageContext: Rate increase notification from current provider

laneContent.backstage: Current provider sends automated rate change notification

significance.description: Trigger event that initiates the switching journey

laneContent.description: Consumer researches how energy switching works, including renter rights and landlord permission requirements

barriers.description: Unclear information about rental property rules for switching — whether landlord approval is needed

designOpportunities: Surface FAQ about tenancy permissions prominently

laneContent.description: Consumer uses comparison websites to find deals, filtering for key criteria like no exit fees and competitive pricing

barriers.description: Confusing tariff structures make like-for-like comparison difficult across providers

designOpportunities: Standardise tariff presentation for easier comparison
Create shareable comparison summaries for multi-person households

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: Understanding of tariff structures, standing charges, unit rates, and exit fee implications
cognitive.supportAvailable: Comparison site calculators standardise some complexity

significance.description: Key research point — tariff selection determines ongoing costs

laneContent.description: Consumer coordinates with all housemates to agree on provider choice and who will be the named account holder

barriers.description: Coordinating decisions with multiple people with different priorities and availability is time-consuming

designOpportunities: Create shareable decision packs consumers can send to housemates
Offer digital voting or approval mechanism for household decisions
laneContent.housemateCoordination: Critical step — needs all housemates to agree on provider and who will be named account holder

significance.description: Gate point — cannot proceed without group consensus

laneContent.description: Consumer and housemates decide whether to proceed with the chosen provider
Consumer navigates to chosen provider's website from comparison site and begins the switch process
laneContent.frontstage: Switch landing page with postcode entry, address lookup
laneContent.backstage: Website validates postcode and retrieves address options

laneContent.description: Consumer enters personal information, property details, current meter readings, and selects tariff and payment method

barriers.description: Phone number is a required field even for consumers who prefer digital-only contact
No clear information about personal liability as account holder in shared properties

laneContent.frontstage: Multi-step registration form with tariff selection, meter reading entry, payment method choice
laneContent.backstage: Form validates inputs, calculates estimated usage based on property size
designOpportunities: Make phone number optional with digital-only contact preference
Provide clear information about shared household liability

significance.description: Commitment point — consumer is investing personal details and taking on account holder responsibility

laneContent.description: Consumer completes online identity verification using driving licence or other ID
laneContent.backstage: System calls Identity Verification API to validate details

laneContent.description: Application is submitted and credit check is performed automatically

barriers.description: No transparency about credit check criteria or how thin credit files are assessed

laneContent.backstage: System submits credit check request to credit bureau API
designOpportunities: Provide upfront guidance on credit check requirements
Offer clear messaging about what happens if check fails

laneContent.description: Credit check result determines whether the application can proceed
Consumer sets up Direct Debit payment and establishes bill-splitting arrangements with housemates

channels.name: Banking app
channels.usageContext: Set up shared pot or payment splitting

designOpportunities: Offer built-in bill-splitting with automated collection from housemates
Integrate with popular payment splitting apps
laneContent.backstage: System validates bank details, sets up Direct Debit mandate

significance.description: Establishes the ongoing payment dynamic — critical for shared households

laneContent.description: Consumer downloads provider app and configures notification and communication preferences
laneContent.frontstage: App onboarding flow with notification preferences, paperless billing toggle, communication channel settings
laneContent.backstage: System saves communication preferences, triggers welcome email sequence

laneContent.description: System sends welcome email with account details, switch timeline, and next steps
laneContent.backstage: Automated welcome sequence triggered, switch request sent to current supplier

laneContent.description: Mandatory 14-day cooling off period during which the consumer can cancel the switch without penalty
laneContent.backstage: System tracks cooling off period, sends progress notifications, coordinates with old supplier

laneContent.description: On switch day, consumer submits final meter readings via the provider app to complete the transfer
laneContent.frontstage: App notification, photo-based meter reading submission
laneContent.backstage: OCR processes meter photo, validates reading, finalises switch with industry systems

significance.description: Transition point — supply officially transfers to new provider

laneContent.description: Consumer receives first bill and can verify charges match the agreed tariff
designOpportunities: Show clear breakdown of charges vs original tariff quote
Provide easy bill-sharing feature for multi-person households

significance.description: Validation point — confirms switch was successful and pricing is as expected

laneContent.description: Consumer sets up ongoing monitoring, usage alerts, and recurring payment collection from housemates

barriers.description: No built-in bill-splitting feature means ongoing administrative burden for the account holder

laneContent.backstage: System configured for paperless billing, usage alerts, and push notifications

laneContent.description: Energy switch complete and ongoing management routine established

condition.description: Housemates agree to proceed with switch

paths.name: Happy path (successful switch)
